description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement at Gioia Tauro for transhipment container ships, car carriers and reefer vessels: hull, hatch and ballast tank readings.
h1: Gioia Tauro: Ultrasonic Gauging for Transhipment Container Ships and Carriers
intro: Gioia Tauro is Italy's largest transhipment hub, a deep-water port in Calabria where container ships exchange boxes before heading across the Mediterranean and beyond. Ships stay at the quay only as long as the cargo operation takes, so Atlantis NDT brings an inspection team from India and plans thickness gauging around the stow plan, concentrating on hatch coamings, ballast tanks and hull areas due for survey.
keywords: car carrier hull inspection gioia tauro

highlights.h: Container ships by the hundred, each briefly alongside
highlights.p: Transhipment calls are short and numerous. A ship rarely lies at the quay for more than a day, so gauging is built around a few spaces the crew can open once cargo handling allows.

highlights.h: Deep-water berths for the largest ships
highlights.p: Gioia Tauro takes some of the largest container ships in the Mediterranean, which carry heavy structure and long hatch coamings. Even a partial programme gives meaningful data for a ship of that size.
The port sits on the main east-west route and close to the Strait of Messina, so ships call here between Suez, Gibraltar and the Black Sea without losing much sea time.

port.h: The port of Gioia Tauro and its place in container shipping
p: Gioia Tauro lies on the Tyrrhenian coast of Calabria, in the plain beyond the Aspromonte hills, a little north of the Strait of Messina. It was built in the 1990s as a purpose-made transhipment port on a coast with few other harbours, and its layout reflects that: a long mole, deep alongside berths and large stacking areas behind them, rather than the compact harbour of a historic town. The approach from the open sea is direct and unobstructed, and there is no tidal gate or lock to plan around. A wide anchorage off the port holds ships waiting for a berth or for orders.

The traffic is mostly boxes in transit. Container ships from Asia and the Middle East discharge here, and feeder ships reload to carry the containers on to ports across the central and western Mediterranean, the Adriatic and North Africa. Many of the ships are very large, with long cargo holds, extensive hatch coaming structure and deep ballast tank arrangements, and carrying such a ship in service puts a high load on hatch covers, cell guides and the structure beneath them. Gioia Tauro also handles ro-ro and vehicle cargo and refrigerated containers, which gives it a mix of ship types beyond the box carriers.

Because the port is a hub, the calendar does not follow the seasons in the way a ferry port does. Calls continue year-round, and for the superintendent the key point is that a ship's visit is short and tied to a cargo plan set by the terminal. That makes advance preparation central: knowing which bays will be accessible and when, which ballast tanks can be emptied, and when the stow plan leaves space clear for the gauging team. Gioia Tauro rewards owners who send a clear request early, because the ship's time alongside is rarely long enough to improvise.

facilities.h: Where thickness gauging can be done at Gioia Tauro
p: Gioia Tauro is a cargo port with no major drydock, and ships needing a docking survey normally continue to a repair yard elsewhere in southern Italy, in Sicily, or to Malta or Naples. The port's value for thickness measurement is the berth. Ships lie at the container quays for the time cargo handling requires, and within that time a limited programme can be completed: hatch coamings and covers, selected ballast tanks that the crew has emptied and ventilated, upper deck plating and, where the stow allows, parts of the hull side accessible from the quay.

Where a ship is waiting for orders at the anchorage, or has been laid up, a launch from the agent can take the team out, though the extent of work depends on the weather and on tanks being gas-free and safe to enter. For ships heading to a yard, readings at Gioia Tauro help the owner set an early steel estimate. The nearby Strait of Messina ports, including Messina itself, have established repair facilities, and a mobilisation by road can cover ships there in the same trip.
list: Container quays — hatch coaming, hatch cover and cell guide area gauging on container ships during the cargo operation
Ballast tanks of transhipment ships — selected tanks emptied and ventilated by the crew, gauged between discharge and sailing
Ro-ro and vehicle carrier berths — ramp, deck and hull side readings on carriers calling for vehicle cargo
Reefer vessels — hull and deck readings on refrigerated cargo ships during port stays
Anchorage off the port — owner's condition work on ships waiting for a berth or on lay-up, using a launch
Messina and the Strait ports — repair yards and layover berths reachable by road, often joined to a Gioia Tauro mobilisation

context.h: Port state control, container-ship structure and the Calabrian setting
p: Ships calling at Gioia Tauro come under Paris MoU port state control, carried out by the Italian Coast Guard, the Guardia Costiera. Container ships are rarely selected for structural reasons alone, but older tonnage on regional feeder services is more exposed, and any structural deficiency recorded in one Italian port will follow a ship to the next. Container ships raise specific structural questions: hatch coaming cracking and wastage, corrosion in ballast tanks adjacent to heated fuel tanks, and fatigue at hatch corners. Thickness records are a practical way to document that a ship is within limits before an inspection occurs.

EU rules add pressure. The Ship Recycling Regulation requires an Inventory of Hazardous Materials for ships calling at EU ports, and EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime apply to the large container ships that make up much of Gioia Tauro's traffic. For owners of older container tonnage, the choice between renewing steel and retiring the ship is increasingly sensitive to emissions rules, and measured thickness provides a sound basis for that decision. Short stops in a hub port are a useful chance to collect this data without disrupting the liner schedule.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Gioia Tauro
jobs.p: Gioia Tauro jobs are short, focused and planned around the terminal's stow plan. We usually see hatch coaming and cover programmes, selected ballast tank readings ahead of a survey, and owner's condition checks on ships waiting at anchor or changing hands. A well-prepared request, with the target spaces and the expected time alongside, lets the team start as soon as the ship is secure and finish with a record the superintendent can use directly.
list: Hatch coaming and hatch cover panel gauging on a container ship during its cargo stop, noting wastage and cracked areas for the surveyor
Ballast tank readings on a transhipment ship after tanks have been emptied and made safe, ahead of a special survey
Ramp and deck plating readings on a car carrier calling for vehicle cargo at the ro-ro berth
Off-hire condition gauging on a feeder ship at the end of a charter, recording hull and hatch cover condition for owner and charterer
Pre-purchase hull gauging of a second-hand container ship at the anchorage off Gioia Tauro

logistics: Lamezia Terme is the nearest commercial airport, with Reggio Calabria also within reach, and Naples or Catania serve as wider gateways; the port is reached by road. The ship's agent arranges the access passes required at the container terminal, which has strict security procedures, and books a launch for ships at the anchorage. The team travels from India and needs Schengen visas, so confirm the ship's expected call early and allow time for visa processing.
vessels: Ships waiting at the anchorage for orders

faqs.q: How long does a container ship normally stay at Gioia Tauro?
faqs.a: Transhipment calls are typically short, often under a day, though that depends on the cargo plan. We therefore ask for the stow plan and expected berth times beforehand, and select spaces that can be opened and gauged within the window rather than a full survey programme.

faqs.q: Can you gauge hatch coamings and covers on a container ship at the quay?
faqs.a: Yes, once cargo handling in the bay allows access. We measure coaming plating, cover panels and the structure at hatch corners, then record any cracking or wastage for the surveyor. The superintendent should confirm which bays will be clear first so the order of work is realistic.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Gioia Tauro for survey work?
faqs.a: The port is a transhipment hub without a significant repair yard. Ships that need docking go to yards in Sicily, Malta, Naples or elsewhere. We take pre-docking readings at Gioia Tauro to give the owner an early steel estimate, then follow the ship if needed.

faqs.q: Can ships at the anchorage be gauged?
faqs.a: Yes, by launch, in suitable weather and with tanks ventilated and certified gas-free by the crew. It suits owner's condition and pre-purchase work. For a class survey record we generally recommend an alongside berth, and we check the purpose of the work before planning.

faqs.q: Can you combine Gioia Tauro with Messina in one mobilisation?
faqs.a: Often, yes. The Strait of Messina ports are reachable by road and have repair yards and layover berths. If an owner has ships in both places in the same week, we sequence the team's time according to each ship's schedule and the scope agreed with its superintendent.
